$$f(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & 0 \leq x < \pi/2 \\ 1 & \pi/2 < x \leq \pi \end{cases}$$

This is a standard problem solvable using the Fourier cosine series expansion. Since the function is defined on $[0, \pi]$, we consider the expansion of $f(x)$ on this interval.

The Fourier cosine series for a function $f(x)$ on $[0, L]$ (here $L=\pi$) is given by:
$$f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)$$
For $L=\pi$:
$$f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos(nx)$$

We need to calculate the coefficients $a_n$.

1. Calculate $a_0$:
$$a_0 = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi} f(x) dx$$
$$a_0 = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 0 dx + \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} 1 dx \right]$$
$$a_0 = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ 0 + [x]_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \right]$$
$$a_0 = \frac{2}{\pi} \left( \pi - \frac{\pi}{2} \right) = \frac{2}{\pi} \left( \frac{\pi}{2} \right) = 1$$
So, $\frac{a_0}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.

2. Calculate $a_n$ for $n \geq 1$:
$$a_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi} f(x) \cos(nx) dx$$
$$a_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 0 \cdot \cos(nx) dx + \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} 1 \cdot \cos(nx) dx \right]$$
$$a_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \cos(nx) dx$$
$$a_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \frac{\sin(nx)}{n} \right]_{\pi/2}^{\pi}$$
$$a_n = \frac{2}{n\pi} \left( \sin(n\pi) - \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{2}\right) \right)$$

Since $\sin(n\pi) = 0$ for integer $n$,
$$a_n = \frac{2}{n\pi} \left( 0 - \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{2}\right) \right) = -\frac{2}{n\pi} \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{2}\right)$$

So $a_{2k} = 0$.

$$f(x) = \frac{1}{2} + \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \left( -\frac{2}{(2k+1)\pi} (-1)^k \right) \cos((2k+1)x)$$
